**I haven’t started any generation or spent generation credits.** I can write the script and plan now, but I can’t verify an exact credit quote: the connected tools don’t expose an account-balance or pricing-check tool. I won’t run a paid generation without giving you a verified cost first.

### Proposed 10-second explainer
Widescreen **16:9**, using a free-plan video model at **480p**, with generated audio enabled.

| Time | Visual | Only on-screen text |
|---|---|---|
| 0–3 seconds | Sun warms a lake; water vapor rises | Evaporation |
| 3–6 seconds | Vapor gathers into a fluffy cloud | Condensation |
| 6–10 seconds | Rain falls back into the lake | Precipitation |

**Friendly voice-over:**  
“Sunlight warms water, and up it goes! It cools into clouds, then falls as rain. That’s the water cycle!”

I’d request exactly those three labels, in that order, with **no title, captions, or other text**. AI-generated lettering and spoken dialogue can be imperfect, so I can’t guarantee exact compliance from a single generation.

### Cheaper, shorter, or smaller?
- **Smaller:** 480p is the free-plan video setting available here; I can’t offer a supported lower-resolution option.
- **Shorter:** A **5-second version** is worth pricing, though it would be rushed with all three stages and narration. I can’t confirm its savings without current rates.
- **Cheapest predictable alternative:** I can give you the storyboard and narration at **zero Magic Hour generation credits**, for assembly in a free slide/video editor. That also gives you reliable, exact labels.

**Cost status: unverified—not zero.** A free plan does not mean generation is credit-free. The safe next step is to check Magic Hour’s quote for **10 seconds, LTX 2.5, 480p, 16:9, audio on**, and compare it with 5 seconds before authorizing either.

## Ready-to-build 10-second explainer

Create a **16:9 widescreen** project in a free slide or video editor. Use simple shapes and animations:

| Timing | Visual and movement | Exact on-screen label |
|---|---|---|
| **0–3 seconds** | Blue lake at the bottom, yellow sun above. Animate three pale-blue wavy arrows rising from the water. | **Evaporation** |
| **3–6 seconds** | The rising vapor gathers into a fluffy white cloud made from overlapping circles. | **Condensation** |
| **6–10 seconds** | Animate blue raindrops falling from the cloud into the lake. | **Precipitation** |

Show **one label at a time**, replacing the previous label. Add no title, subtitles, credits, or other on-screen text.

### Friendly voice-over
Read warmly at a steady pace:

> “Sunlight warms water, and up it goes! It cools into clouds, then falls as rain. That’s the water cycle!”

Start the first sentence at **0 seconds**, the second at **3 seconds**, and “then falls as rain” around **6 seconds**.

### Assemble and export
1. Make three scenes lasting **3, 3, and 4 seconds**.
2. Record the narration using your phone or the editor’s microphone.
3. Use simple motion animations; avoid transitions that change the total duration.
4. Export as a **10-second, 16:9 MP4**, at 480p if available.

This is a build-ready plan, **not a rendered video**, so there’s no download link.
